title: Trivial scalar condensed coefficients are acyclic for pro-prime-to-ell groups
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use a small coherent profinite site in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $K$ let $\mathcal A_K(C_F)$ be the category of internal $C_F$-modules with $C_F$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline K(S)=C(S,K)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and let $R\Gamma_K$ be the ordinary total right derived invariant-submodule functor [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Give the regular module $C_F$ the trivial $K$-action. If every finite continuous quotient of $K$ has order prime to $\ell$, the canonical augmentation
$$\eta_{K,F}:C_F[0]\longrightarrow R\Gamma_K(C_F[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. Here $[0]$ places a module in cochain degree zero, and the augmentation is induced by the inclusion of invariant sections into an injective resolution, with $\Gamma_K(C_F)=C_F$. This concerns ordinary internal condensed modules and the noncomplete norm-topological $\Omega$, with no completion or restriction to locally constant functions.
